rules.rule: Check for urgent abnormal thoughts or behaviour conditions
rules.problem: Low: it also checks for the dementia findings, which come from the non-urgent "Approach" section, under an "urgent" title. Harmless, because the dementia rule consumes them.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible stroke in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: "New" and "asymmetric" are dropped. Only Sudden onset is kept, so symmetric deficits trigger the rule. "Possible" correctly matches "consider stroke".

rules.rule: Diagnose possible TIA in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: Same as stroke: the asymmetric/unilateral qualifier is missing.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable delirium in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: The AND of fluctuating consciousness and temperature >= 38 matches the page box literally.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable mania in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: "Reckless" from the page box is not encoded (candidates: "Disinhibited behavior" or "Reckless character"). The OR of single features makes any one item, e.g. irritable alone, give probable mania. That is a broad reading of a box with no "any of".

rules.rule: Diagnose probable psychosis in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: The structure (lack of insight AND >=1 of) is faithful, but "disorganised behaviour" is missing and "disorganised speech" is mapped to an articulation concept.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable stimulant drug intoxication in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: The page box is a cluster with no "≥ 1 of" (contrast the psychosis box, which says it). The rule ORs every sign, so nausea alone, sweating alone, restlessness alone or BP >= 140/90 alone gives PROBABLE stimulant intoxication. It also overlaps heavily with the withdrawal signs. An any2 or a substance-use anchor would be more faithful.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable alcohol intoxication in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: Any single sign (e.g. unsteady gait or incoordination alone, without a smell of alcohol) gives probable alcohol intoxication. The page lists a cluster with no "any of". Consider requiring the smell of alcohol, or any2.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable alcohol/drug withdrawal in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: The structure (stopped/reduced AND >=1 sign) is good. Reduced drug intake is missing ("Reduced drugs misuse"), and "known user" is only implicit.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable poisoning in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: Exposure to the root "Substance" concept makes the rule fire on any recorded substance exposure.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible dementia in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: The onset >= time_ago 6 months direction is correct ("at least 6 months") and "possible" matches "consider". Only the Difficulty coping concept is imprecise.

rules.rule: Urgent: abnormal thoughts or behaviour of sudden or recent onset
rules.problem: It matches the red-box header and its two criteria. Urgent is justified by "Give urgent attention".

summary: The most consequential problem: the stimulant-intoxication and alcohol-intoxication rules OR every listed sign, so a single nonspecific finding (nausea, sweating, restlessness, raised BP, unsteady gait) yields a PROBABLE diagnosis, although the page gives a cluster with no "any of". Stroke/TIA drop "asymmetric", and Poisoning uses the root "Substance" concept. Smaller concept issues: disorganised speech mapped to an articulation finding, reduced drug intake missing, "Difficulty coping" instead of functional decline, and "reckless" missing from mania.
